newsitem.title: FRANCE: France increasing reinforcements to Congo.
newsitem.headline: France increasing reinforcements to Congo.

text.p: France is sending 800 extra troops to Brazzaville to reinforce some 450 already in the strife-torn capital of Congo, a defence ministry spokeswoman said on Monday.
The spokeswoman said 400 soldiers were flying in from mainland France and another 400 from Chad. "We'll have 1,200 men on the ground tomorrow," she said.
The spokeswoman said 400 marines flew from Castres in southern France, and 200 Foreign legionnaires and 200 marines were flying in from N'djamena, the capital of Chad.

French troops on Monday flew 460 French residents from Brazzaville to safety in Libreville in neighbouring Gabon, and 100 more would follow later in the day, she said. Those evacuated were likely to fly on to Paris.

The reinforcements will join foreign legionnaires who have been in Brazzaville for several weeks in case they were needed to evacuate foreigners from Kinshasa following the takeover of President Laurent Kabila from ousted president Mobutu Sese Seko.
Fighting with heavy weapons resumed in Brazzaville on Monday as forces loyal to President Pascal Lissouba recaptured part of central Brazzaville from ex-president Denis Sassou Nguesso's militia.
